title: Instruction release checklist (scratch)
content:
Quick notes + working checklist for shipping 'instruction' updates (prompts, instruction templates, packaged instruction packs) that teams can safely deploy to production. Purpose: reduce regressions from prompt changes, clarify owner responsibilities, provide telemetry gating and automatic rollback hooks.

Context / motivation:
- We ship a lot of instruction tweaks (tone, system message tweaks, constraint tokens) and sometimes see downstream regressions or user confusion after a change.
- Engineers want a lightweight, repeatable process that doesn't feel like full product release for every prompt tweak.
- Product + DX want auditability + provenance for who changed which instruction and why.

Non-goals (for this scratch):
- This is not full legal review flow for PII-sensitive prompts (that's a separate compliance checklist).
- Not trying to replace rollouts for model binaries or infra changes. Focus is on instruction/content surface.

Stakeholders:
- Owner (author) — accountable for checklist items and monitoring window
- Reviewer (peer) — quick QA + approval (functional test, edge-case tests)
- Observability lead — ensures telemetry and alert hooks exist
- PM — approves UX/behavior changes for customers

User stories (short):
- As an engineer, I want to publish an instruction change that can be auto-rolled back if the error rate or latency regresses beyond a threshold.
- As a product manager, I want to see a diff and can preview differences on a sample prompt set before approving.
- As an SRE, I want the change to include a canary percentage and automatic fallback to previous instruction if SLOs break.

Acceptance criteria (minimal for shipping):
- Diff available in UI/CLI and attached to the change set (who, why, change notes).
- Test harness: can run instruction-change against canonical prompt set (<= 200 prompts) and produce pass/fail on smoke tests.
- Telemetry: record InstructionChangeSubmitted, InstructionChangeCanary, InstructionChangeRollback events with tags (owner, change_id, canary_pct, model_slot).
- Canary config supported via API: canary_percent (0-100), window_minutes, metric_thresholds (error_rate, latency_p95, nlu_fallback_rate).
- Automatic rollback: If any metric breaches configured thresholds during canary window, revert to previous active instruction and post rollback event.

Suggested minimal checklist (for small changes):
- [ ] Title + short rationale
- [ ] Owner assigned + reviewer assigned
- [ ] Diff created and human-readable notes
- [ ] Smoke tests added (instructions + 12 representative prompts)
- [ ] Canary config specified (default 5% / 30m)
- [ ] Telemetry hooks present (see event list above)
- [ ] Rollback threshold values set (or accept defaults)
- [ ] Concurrency/cost estimate noted (expected tokens/requests incremental)
- [ ] Security/compliance quick-check: any PII or data collection changes? If yes, attach compliance ticket
- [ ] Postmortem template prefilled in case of rollback

Telemetry & metrics (quick sketch):
- Events: InstructionChangeCreated(change_id, owner, model, target_route), InstructionChangeCanary(change_id, pct), InstructionChangeCanaryResult(change_id, metric, baseline, current, breached(Boolean)), InstructionChangeRollback(change_id, reason)
- Baselines: take 7d historical for latency_p95, error_rate, semantic-quality (if available via evals)
- Quality signal ideas: eval delta on golden prompt set (BLEU-ish or embedding-sim + threshold), user satisfaction proxy (session continuation rate), explicit user feedback flags

Rollout examples / CLI mock (sketch):
- rdxctl instruction push --file updated-instruction.yaml --title "Reduce verbosity for summarizer" --canary 5 --window 30 --rollback-metric latency_p95>1200ms
- rdxctl instruction promote --change-id C1234 --to 100
- rdxctl instruction status C1234 --watch

Preview & test harness notes:
- Build a lightweight preview UI that runs new instruction vs old on a sample set and highlights token diffs + top-k completions. Keep it offline (no production calls) until reviewer approves.
- Smoke tests should be runnable in CI with a small local model (or recorded responses) to avoid cost.

Migration / tagging model:
- Tag instructions by compat-level: compatible, potentially-breaking, breaking. Only allow canary <100% for 'potentially-breaking' and require explicit approval for 'breaking'.
- Provide a migration plan field (free text) if instruction changes affect downstream parsing / structured outputs.

Open questions / risks (to resolve in follow-ups):
- How to measure semantic quality for arbitrary instructions cheaply? (embedding-similarity on golden set? rule-based heuristics?)
- Who has final approval for UX-facing instruction changes (PM vs owner)?
- Interaction with model rollouts: if model variant changes at the same time as instruction, complexity multiplies — enforce single-diff deployments or require paired rollouts.
- Cost: frequent smoke-run + canaries add to infra costs — need budget guardrail per team.

Back-of-envelope timeline for MVP (owner-run):
- Week 0: prototype diff + CLI push, basic telemetry events wired (InstructionChangeCreated/Canary/Rollback)
- Week 1: add smoke-test harness + preview UI, default canary support
- Week 2: automatic rollback hook + simple postmortem template generation
- Week 3: soft launch with 2 pilot teams (DX + a customer internal team)

Quick TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Spike telemetry event shapes and wire into console events stream (owner: Mika)
- [ ] Draft CLI UX and wire push/promote/status commands (owner: Sam)
- [ ] Build simple smoke-table of canonical prompts (owner: Leah)
- [ ] Draft guardrail docs + who-approves matrix (owner: PM)

Notes to self / brainstorm bits:
- Could we allow instruction bundles with versioned assets (e.g., templates + example inputs + tests) so reviewers can reproduce locally? Seems valuable.
- Consider a low-friction license that marks internal-only vs public instructions — useful for community packs later.
- Fancy: integrate a lightweight synthetic user (heuristic agent) to run conversational flows for behavior regression detection. Maybe later.

Attachments / links (placeholders):
- "example-instruction-template.yaml" (should live in GH PR)
- Confluence: governance doc (TBD)

End of scratch — keep this free-form. Will iterate into a short PRD once we validate telemetry feasibility.
